reason: The storm may cut solar power, so putting the charged reserve at the shutdown controls seems like a direct way to prepare the station.
expectation: I expect the station to switch to its emergency reserve, though other shutdown steps may still be needed.

alternatives.reason: The outdoor water line will lose heat, so I considered addressing it first, but the station's power reserve seems more immediate.
Moving the heat store could protect the garden, but the current goal is to put the station on reserve.

effect: The reserve now supplies essential loads, while the fuel plant and garden circulation are off. The nook has low-power outlets for survival equipment.
reaction: The loss of circulation makes protecting the garden feel more urgent.
reason: The outdoor line will lose its heat, so I want to address it at the shutdown controls before turning to the garden.
expectation: I expect the line to be isolated or otherwise prepared for the unheated period, though I don't know exactly what the controls will do.

alternatives.reason: Moving the charged heat store into the nook could help protect the plants, but the exposed line also needs attention.

effect: The outdoor line is drained and isolated, with its pump and thaw checks on essential power. The next goal is to move both troughs into the nook.
reaction: Draining the line is a reassuringly practical response to losing its heat.
reason: The troughs need to move into the warm nook, so I’ll start with the lettuce.
expectation: I expect the lettuce trough to be placed inside the nook; the potato trough will probably still need moving.

alternatives.reason: The charged heat store could warm the nook, but the current goal specifically calls for moving the troughs.
The potato trough also needs shelter; I have no clear reason to move it before the lettuce.

effect: The lettuce is sheltered with its own reservoir, and the potato trough still needs to move.
reaction: I like the practical detail of capping the couplings and keeping the bed level.
reason: Moving the potato trough addresses the remaining part of the current goal.
expectation: I expect the potato trough to be placed in the nook alongside the lettuce, though its supports may need attention.

alternatives.reason: The heat store should help keep the nook warm, but I want to finish moving both troughs first.

effect: Both troughs are now sheltered in the nook, with their reservoirs and the potato bed’s cover and support intact.
reaction: It is satisfying that the two beds fit without sacrificing the potato support.
reason: The charged heat store is the only available combination, and placing it in the nook should help keep the sheltered beds warm.
expectation: I expect the heat store to release warmth near the troughs, though I don't know whether further steps will be needed to protect them.

effect: The heat store completed the buffered growing nook and the chapter’s remaining goal.
reaction: The completion is reassuring, though I would have liked a little more detail about how the heat store protects the beds.

mostWorthwhile.text: Draining and isolating the outdoor water line was the most worthwhile action: it made the response to losing heat concrete and explained how the line could later be brought back into service.

leastWorthwhile.text: Moving the second trough felt somewhat repetitive after moving the first, although its different depth and supports added useful detail.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the garden’s normal circulation stopped when the station switched to reserve, making the nook’s low-power outlets relevant.

arbitrary.text: Placing the heat store was sensible, but the result gave little detail about its role, and it was the only combination available at that point.

continue.text: Yes. I would choose to continue to learn how the station and garden fare through the storm and what the lab makes of the articulated body.
